title: ci: declare the action reference convention and gate the odd one out
body:
Fixes #8465

Writes down the convention this repository uses for action references, and makes it checkable. **No action reference is changed by this PR, in either direction.**

## The re-derived census, with its control

Re-measured on a re-fetched `origin/main` at `96cf3d2acdb77afd3667c23c63e3c7490b04529b` (the card measured `1706d8be4`; the tree has moved since). Enumeration and reading both come from the same checkout of that commit.

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| distinct action references in `.github/workflows/**` | **13** |
| of those, SHA-pinned (`grep -cP '@[0-9a-f]{40}$'` over the list) | **1** — `actions/stale@e00e804f...` |
| positive control in the same run, `actions/checkout@v7` | **found** (count 1 in the distinct list) |
| total `uses:` occurrences / workflow files | 107 / 34 before this PR, 109 / 35 after |

The card's and triage's numbers both reproduce exactly. Triage's noise warning also reproduces: the `changesets/action@v1` with a trailing backtick sits inside a comment, and both the census and the gate strip comment lines before scanning, so it is not a 14th reference.

## What landed, and why there

- **`.github/workflows/action-ref-convention.yml`** — the convention, stated in the workflow header. This is triage's "a README or comment under `.github/workflows/`", in the form this repository already uses for exactly this purpose (`control-bytes.yml` and `changeset-guard.yml` both carry their rationale as a header at length).
- **`scripts/check-action-ref-convention.mjs`** — the gate, so the convention is enforced rather than prose that drifts.
- **`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`** — a section plus an inventory row. Not optional: `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` fails when a workflow has no heading naming its file.
- **`scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs`** — the new check classified into `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, because `dependabot-merge-gate.test.ts` requires the three buckets to partition every check a PR produces.

**A `.github/workflows/README.md` was considered and rejected.** objectui#3724 deleted `.github/WORKFLOWS.md` for being hand-maintained, linked from nowhere and pinned by nothing, and `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` still asserts it stays deleted with the note that "a new inventory under a different name evades it". A fresh unlinked doc under `.github/` is that same shape. `AGENTS.md` was never a candidate: it is governed surface.

## The convention

**Default spelling: a floating major tag, `owner/action@vN`.**

**An exception is marked by an entry in `DECLARED_EXCEPTIONS`**, carrying the workflow file, the action path, the issue that owns the decision, and a real reason. That is the only form an exception takes. A trailing `# v9.0.0`-style comment beside a ref is a version *hint*, not a reason, and the gate does not read it as one — which matters, because the ref at the centre of this card already has one.

The exception mechanism is the point, not the default. The defect was an **unmarked, unverified** exception; a convention that names a default but gives an exception no visible form leaves the same hole.

## Why the default is the tag, and what that does not mean

Because that is what the tree already was: 12 of 13, and the repository's one deliberately reasoned per-ref pin — `changesets/action@v1`, held by `scripts/__tests__/changeset-release-action-ref-pin.test.ts` against two properties of v1's source — is itself a tag. Declaring it moves no reference and closes no door.

**This is not a ruling against SHA pinning.** SHA pinning is normally the *more* secure spelling and supply-chain guidance recommends it. Per triage, moving this repository's pinning posture wholesale is a supply-chain decision that belongs on its own card, and the reverse — quietly turning the SHA into a tag — is equally out of bounds. The gate's failure text says both, so a future reader cannot mistake the default for a verdict.

## What the gate deliberately does not do

It checks **spelling, not resolvability**. A SHA pointing at no commit and one pointing at a real commit are indistinguishable without the network. That is the honest boundary: what failed in #8465 was that the odd ref had no reason attached and no second instance to compare against, and both of those are checkable offline.

## Interaction with #8126 — please read before that card lands

`stale.yml` is **not touched** by this PR. Its ref is recorded as a declared exception owned by objectui#8126, so this gate is green on a tree it did not break without pre-empting what that card writes there.

That entry carries a staleness check, like every other escape hatch in this repository (`KNOWN_OFFENDERS`, `DOCUMENTATION_EXEMPT`, `MUST_SUBSCRIBE_MERGE_GROUP`). **Consequence, stated plainly: if #8126 changes that ref to a tag, this gate goes red on that PR until the now-unused entry is deleted** — a one-line deletion, with the failure text saying exactly that. That is deliberate. Triage's requirement was that whatever #8126 writes, the reason survives in the tree; an entry nobody is forced to look at would not satisfy it.

## Evidence

**Ablation — the gate can fail.** Mutation proved on disk *before* the run, restore proved by state, never by an exit code:

```
HEAD blob: 43f7cb1c39fe4e008be75601a7bcc941d8baf266
pre-mutation  'uses: actions/checkout@v7' occurrences: 1
post-mutation injected SHA occurrences : 1
post-mutation removed  tag occurrences : 0
blob now: 594d9e8d27e8c638a440cda4603d9825afe0de24   (differs from HEAD blob)
MUTATED_GATE_EXIT=1
  control-bytes.yml:69  actions/checkout@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567   [sha]
RESTORE: blob after restore 43f7cb1c... matches HEAD blob YES
         git diff HEAD -- control-bytes.yml  =>  empty
RESTORED_GATE_EXIT=0
```

The mutation script carried a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restore with absolute paths throughout.

**Tests.** All figures below are on the final commit.

```
pnpm exec vitest run scripts/            122 files, 3651 tests passed
pnpm type-check:scripts                  exit 0
pnpm lint:root --format json             279 files, 0 errors, 32 warnings, exit 0
node scripts/check-action-ref-convention.mjs
  OK  109 action reference(s) in 35 workflow file(s), 13 distinct;
      0 off-convention and undeclared, 0 stale exception(s);
      control `actions/checkout` present: true
node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs     exit 0 (6747 tracked text files)
node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs
  exit 0 — no source or published contract of a released package changed, so no changeset is owed
node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test (all changed paths)
  NOT GOVERNED — 5 paths checked against 5 governed surfaces; none matched
```

`lint:root` is the scan that covers `scripts/`; it ran over its full population rather than a narrowed subset, so no narrowing claim is being made. ESLint here is not type-aware (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`).

The new suite is 16 tests, including four that assert the gate's red branches fire, one that reproduces the census with a second independent parser and requires the two to agree, and one that asserts prose inside comments is never counted as a reference.

**Note:** `Bundle Analysis` is red on every PR that triggers it right now — objectui#8541, not this PR, and not a required check.
